content.user_title: Upgrade Dependencies With Focused Migration Checks
content.value_statement: Dependency upgrades can introduce breaking changes and obscure existing failures. This skill guides focused migrations through release notes, baseline comparisons, minimal edits, and rollback reporting.
actual_capabilities: Guides installed-version checks using lockfiles and target-version queries using the project package manager.
Directs review of intervening release notes for breaking changes, runtime requirements, changed defaults, and deprecations.
Maps changed APIs to affected files using codebase searches before editing.
Scopes manifest, lockfile, and code updates to one dependency and required peers.
Compares installation, build, test, lint, and type-check results before and after the upgrade.
Structures upgrade reports with source links, applied changes, verification results, warnings, and rollback guidance.
limitations: Provides workflow instructions, not a bundled upgrade engine or package-specific migration database.
Requires an assistant with repository access, command execution, and access to relevant release documentation.
Cannot guarantee compatibility when release notes are unavailable or project tests leave behavior uncovered.
Requires user approval before changing minimum runtime or peer versions; major-version runtime checks depend on feasibility.

use_cases.title: Update an application library
use_cases.description: Inspect release notes, identify affected APIs, update one package, and compare project checks against the baseline.

use_cases.title: Prepare a framework migration
use_cases.description: Map major-version changes, identify runtime and peer requirements, and request approval before expanding the upgrade scope.

use_cases.title: Document a security-related upgrade
use_cases.description: Upgrade an affected dependency and cite an advisory only when official documentation supports the security claim.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an upgrade target
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the installed version of [package] and identify the latest release. Summarize relevant release notes without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the current version and upgrade target.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a focused upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade [package] to [target version]. Record baseline checks, review release notes, update affected code, and compare verification results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: execute a single dependency upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a major migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the migration of [framework] from [current version] to [target version]. Map breaking APIs and request approval for runtime or peer changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess a major release before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve conflicts with evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [package] upgrade conflicts without overriding dependency constraints. Present conflict output, options, official advisory evidence if applicable, verification gaps, and rollback guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate dependency conflicts and security claims.

output_examples.input: Show an example planning report for a major dependency upgrade.
output: Illustrative plan: confirm the installed version from the lockfile and select an explicit target.
Review intervening release notes and list affected API usages with file references.
Record baseline checks before changes and request approval for required runtime or peer upgrades.
Report verification differences and a rollback option after implementation.

output_examples.input: Show an example response when an upgrade requires an unapproved runtime change.
output: Illustrative status: paused pending approval for the required runtime change.
Present the documented minimum runtime and explain why it expands the requested scope.
Ask whether to approve the runtime change or consider another target version.
Identify checks not completed and avoid claiming the migration passed.

best_practices: Start with a clean working tree and record existing failures before changing dependencies.
Use the project package manager for manifest and lockfile updates, and cite release notes for applicable changes.
Compare verification results with the baseline and document skipped checks, remaining warnings, and rollback steps.
anti_patterns: Running a blanket dependency update when the request concerns one package.
Combining an upgrade with unrelated refactoring or changing runtime requirements without approval.
Skipping failing tests, loosening version ranges, or overriding conflicts to conceal compatibility problems.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Practical execution requires repository access and the tools needed for the project.

faq.question: Does this skill include an automated upgrade script?
faq.answer: No. It contains a Markdown workflow that guides an assistant through planning, edits, verification, and reporting.

faq.question: Can it upgrade multiple dependencies together?
faq.answer: It focuses on one dependency or a tightly coupled group, including required peers. It explicitly rejects blanket updates.

faq.question: What happens when release notes are missing?
faq.answer: The workflow requires stating that release notes are unavailable and treating the upgrade as higher risk.

faq.question: Will it change runtime requirements automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requires stopping and asking before changing minimum runtime or peer versions.

faq.question: Can it prove that an upgrade fixes a vulnerability?
faq.answer: It permits security claims only when supported by an official advisory or release notes. It does not provide an independent vulnerability scanner.
